newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County administrator unveils $11.9 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County administrator unveils $11.9 bln budget.

text.p: Los Angeles County's chief administrator on Monday proposed an $11.97 billion 1997-1998 budget that calls for 1,200 job reductions in the health services department.

County Chief Administrative Officer David Janssen said his proposed spending plan -- $173 million smaller than the current budget -- is balanced, but warned that the county's financial condition remains "precarious."

"Although the Board of Supervisors has made significant reductions in budget expenditures and employee count, we continue to struggle with budget gaps and an inability to meet critical needs," Janssen said in a statement.
"We are rapidly approaching the point where the only solution to the ongoing problem is in the hands of the state and federal government," Janssen said.

Janssen's proposed budget calls for the loss of an estimated 1,200 positions in the county Health Services Department due to downsizing. The county would add, however, hundreds of social service and sheriff's department jobs.

The budget includes 304 new positions in the department of public social services to help welfare recipients find jobs and 718 new sheriff's department jobs to fully operate the county's Twin Towers jail in downtown Los Angeles.
Janssen warned that several factors could undermine his budget plan, including fluctuations in state funding and unexpected costs associated with welfare reform.
The budget does not include any funds for pay raises. Most county employees have not had a raise for three years, and for many groups it has been four and five years.
"Although salary increases continue to be a high priority, at this time there simply is no money to pay for them," Janssen said.
